newsitem.title: CANADA: CRICKET-RAIN PREVENTS PLAY IN CANADIAN CRICKET SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN PREVENTS PLAY IN CANADIAN CRICKET SUNDAY.

text.p: Persistent rain made play impossible Sunday, forcing the second match postponement of the international cricket series between Pakistan and India in Toronto.
The five-match Sahara Cup series had been scheduled to get underway this weekend with games on Saturday and Sunday at the Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling club.
However heavy rain started falling in the region on Friday, flooding the ground which boasts one of Canada's few turf cricket wickets.
Officials postponed Saturday's match, rescheduling it for Monday. They had hoped to start the series on Sunday but heavy showers overnight made the ground unplayable.
That match will now be played on Tuesday.
Organisers remain optimistic the series will finally get underway on Monday.

"All we need is a little sun, the ground drains really well and the pitch has been covered throughout the rain," said Ravi Krishnan, a spokesman for the International Management Group which organised the event with International Cricket Council sanction.

More than 5,000 spectators, mostly cricket enthusiasts from the large, local Indian, Pakistani and West Indies communities are expected to pack the small, but immaculately kept ground in Toronto's north when play finally gets underway.
Weather permitting, matches will now be played on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday with the final two encounters next Saturday and Sunday.
